verdicts.strongest_argument: The underlying data is an official, free, monthly-updated US Mint dataset (bullion-american-eagle-silver.csv), and the specific 'zero in May 2026, first full month in the program's history' headline was published on at least two bullion trade sites and folded into the routine CoinNews monthly sales coverage, with the May figure public in early June and the June figure in early July. My own arithmetic check against the published 'roughly 8.8 million ounces YTD through June, ahead of 2025 thanks entirely to a big January' confirms the hunter's monthly splits exactly (8.18M in Jan-Mar plus 380.5k + 0 + 260k = 8.82M), which also means the reconciliation is already sitting in public copy. Critically, the price moved on this story while it was happening: GOLD hit its 52-week high of $66.70 on 2026-02-09 and traded down to a $37.01 low in July, a 44% drawdown that maps almost exactly onto the five-month decline in Eagle orders and the premium collapse. Against that, Silver Eagle bullion is a proxy rather than a P&L line for this company - all Authorized Purchasers together took 8.18M coins in fiscal Q3 while Gold.com alone sold 34.6M ounces of silver that quarter, so the company's own Eagle exposure is single-digit percent of its silver ounces. What I do concede is genuinely new: nobody has published the link from zero Mint bullion orders to Sunshine Minting's silver-blank business, which Gold.com only consolidated on 2026-04-02 and which therefore carries a full quarter of cost against a customer that ordered nothing in May.

prior_publication.what_it_says: US Mint sold zero 1oz bullion Silver Eagles in May 2026, the first full-month zero in the program's history and the bottom of a five-month decline that began in February.
Independent second write-up of the same May 2026 zero print and what it means for retail silver buyers.
Routine monthly US Mint bullion sales coverage covering the June 2026 data, noting YTD bullion Silver Eagle sales of roughly 8.8 million ounces through June and a downtrend since February.
The primary source itself - the Mint publishes monthly American Eagle silver bullion sales as a free CSV.

Gold.com acquired the remaining 55.10% of Sunshine Minting on 2026-04-02, taking weekly finished-product capacity above 3 million ounces - so the consolidation date and the added cost base are public.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Spot $43.66 against a 52-week high of $66.70 set 2026-02-09 (pct_from_52w_high -31.93 in the baseline); the stock traded to $37.01 in July. A 40-44% drawdown through exactly the window in which Eagle orders fell to zero is the market pricing this collapse, not ignoring it. Skew is essentially flat at +0.59 vol points and put/call OI is 0.29, so the option market is not paying up for a downside surprise on top of it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosed Gold.com share of Authorized Purchaser Eagle volume, or Sunshine blank revenue large enough to be a named line item, would move this toward the 20s.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the best mechanism in the set - premium over spot times ounces really is this company's gross profit, not the metal price - and the specific magnitude (19.16% peak on 2026-02-17 collapsing to a 5.30% trough on 2026-04-24) is not drawn out anywhere I could find. But premium compression as the driver of A-Mark/Gold.com margins is a long-established, management-narrated theme rather than a discovery: the company's own fiscal Q1 2026 release described 'subdued demand and historically tight premium spreads', Northland previously downgraded the stock explicitly on 'softened demand, premium compression, and elevated gold and silver prices', and on the 2026-05-06 call Greg Roberts told the market directly that premiums had 'normalized' from the January-February extreme and that volume had 'retreat[ed] from where we were in January and February'. So the direction, the mechanism and management's own framing were all on the tape four months ago, and the sell-side responded by cutting the June-quarter estimate to $0.94-0.96 against Q3's $2.09 - a 55% sequential decline already embedded in the number. The premium series itself lives on a niche retail price-tracking site but is trivially observable to anyone who looks at a dealer page, which is what makes it 'published somewhere obscure' rather than private. The part of the claim that runs into July and August 2026 does not reach this print at all - that is fiscal Q1 2027 - and it directly contradicts GOLD-2#2's reading of the same July data.

prior_publication.what_it_says: CEO Greg Roberts on the record: premiums have normalized from peak and 'we have had a bit of volume retreat from where we were in January and February' - i.e. management pre-flagged the fiscal Q4 environment.
The company's own fiscal Q1 2026 release describes subdued demand and historically tight premium spreads, establishing premium compression as a disclosed, recurring risk narrative.
Northland downgrade citing softened demand, premium compression and elevated metal prices as the reason results missed - the exact mechanism, already used by a covering analyst to change a rating.

The public premium-history series the finding is built on (fetch returned 403 for me; treated as snippet-confirmed via the same site's May-zero article, which quotes 12-20% typical major-dealer premiums).

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The premium peak on 2026-02-17 sits one week after the 52-week high of $66.70 (2026-02-09) and the trough on 2026-04-24 sits inside the slide toward the $37.01 July low. The stock's premium-driven earnings power and the premium series moved together, in public, with a lag of weeks not quarters. Consensus at $0.94-0.96 versus Q3's $2.09 is the sell-side having already written the compression down.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus was built off Q3-like premiums rather than the compressed level - for instance a covering analyst note dated after 2026-05-06 still modelling a Q3-type gross margin - would drop this into the 20s.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the one finding here that is genuinely obscure - a B2B e-commerce intelligence vendor page, not a financial publication, and I found no financial-press pickup of it. I will not pretend it is priced. What I will attack is whether it matters. First, the reliability: Grips puts jmbullion.com at $716.5M of 2025 revenue, which is an order of magnitude below the scale implied by Gold.com's actual DTC segment (JM Bullion alone was 27% of a $176.6M consolidated gross profit quarter), so this is a web-traffic-modelled figure with a large and unknown error term, and the Similarweb rank data it is paired with is free and public to anyone. Second, the window: the stated data period is July 2026, which is fiscal Q1 2027, not the quarter being reported, and the 'trailing three months versus preceding three months' comparison spans May-July against February-April, so only two of the three months sit inside fiscal Q4. Third, the mechanism: for a bullion dealer, revenue is metal price times ounces, and a 24% revenue decline into a period of sharply higher silver spot tells you about volume but says almost nothing about gross profit, which is set by premium. A 3% month-on-month traffic dip and a global-rank move from 18,648 to 20,259 is noise at this company's scale.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Third-party estimate of jmbullion.com at $66.4M July 2026 revenue, $716.5M for 2025, and a 24% decline over the trailing three months versus the preceding three - publicly viewable but on a vendor marketing page, not a financial outlet.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None specific. GOLD closed July at $39.35 after a $37.01 low and then rallied 11.85% in August to a $47.25 high, which is not the shape of a market absorbing a JM Bullion revenue shock - it is the shape of a market trading the gold price.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Grips or Similarweb series restricted to April-June 2026 showing the same 24% decline, cross-checked against a disclosed JM Bullion ounce count, would justify 15 or lower.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is in the company's own press release of 2026-05-06 - 9M gross profit $342.8M, Q3 $176.6M, 9M net income $70.2M, Q3 $59.5M, Q3 SG&A $78.0M, Q3 interest $19.0M - and I verified all six against the release itself. The derived H1 figures are two subtractions on numbers that were covered the same day by Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha, Globe and Mail and StockTitan, and the 9M diluted EPS of $2.65 against Q3's $2.09 puts the whole H1 EPS at $0.56 in the release's own summary table, so the 'H1 was nearly nothing' point is legible from the headline EPS line without any arithmetic at all. The Sunshine cost base was announced by GlobeNewswire on 2026-04-02. Most damaging: the exact framing this finding claims as its edge - that Q3 may have been an unrepeatable spike and the estimate is fragile - is in wire copy published today, before the print, by Investing.com: investors will scrutinise 'whether last quarter's performance represents a sustainable baseline or an opportunistic spike that will prove difficult to replicate.' And the 'lone estimate' argument cuts against the hunter, not for them: one or two estimates on a $1.27B-cap name with 71% ATM implied vol and an 8.87% event-implied move means nobody is anchored on $0.94 tightly enough for a miss to be a surprise. I do concede that no published source has put a specific number on the downside case, and $0.19 versus $0.94 would be a large miss - which is why this is 78 and not 90.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The source of every input: Q3 gross profit $176.6M, net income $59.5M, diluted EPS $2.09, SG&A $78.0M, interest $19.0M; 9M gross profit $342.8M, net income $70.2M, diluted EPS $2.65.

Pre-print wire preview: consensus $0.94 EPS on $5.67B revenue, and the explicit question of whether Q3 was a sustainable baseline or an opportunistic spike difficult to replicate as gold volatility moderates.
Sunshine Minting consolidated from the start of fiscal Q4, so the added full-quarter cost base is public and dated.
Management explicitly declined to guide Q4 SG&A, interest or Sunshine integration cost, and flagged volume retreat from the Jan-Feb peak.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Consensus of $0.94-0.96 versus Q3's realised $2.09 is already a 55% sequential cut, and the stock is 31.9% below its 52-week high with realised 20d vol of 53.1%. The 8.87% event-implied move on a flat skew (+0.59 vol points, put/call OI 0.29) says the market expects a big move without expecting a particular sign - consistent with knowing the estimate is unreliable rather than trusting it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated post-2026-05-06 sell-side note that visibly builds $0.94 off Q3-like unit economics rather than H1-like ones would make the fragility argument new and pull this under 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the World Gold Council's flagship quarterly publication, released 2026-07-30 and picked up by Coin World and Seeking Alpha among others; Gold Demand Trends is the single most-read demand dataset in the sector and its numbers are in every gold desk's note within a day. Worse for the finding, the WGC's own framing of the same 307.1t number is the opposite of the hunter's: it describes bar and coin investment as having 'held steady year-over-year at 307 tonnes', consistent with the 305t five-year quarterly average from Q4 2020 to Q3 2025, and explicitly reads it as 'a return to more typical levels of buying following two extraordinarily strong quarters'. The -36% sequential figure is arithmetically right but is the mirror image of a Q1 that the publisher itself calls extraordinary, so the magnitude is not merely contested - the primary source contests it. Global bar-and-coin tonnage is also a poor proxy for this company, which is a US wholesaler and DTC retailer whose margin is premium not tonnage, and the WGC publishes a separate US Focus report that would be the right cut. The remainder of the finding restates GOLD-1#0's Silver Eagle zero and GOLD-1#1's premium trough rather than adding to them.

prior_publication.what_it_says: WGC Q2 2026 investment chapter: bar and coin investment 307t, held steady year-over-year, in line with the 305t five-year quarterly average, described as a return to typical levels after two extraordinarily strong quarters.
Trade-press coverage of the WGC Gold Demand Trends release.
Seeking Alpha republication/analysis of Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026 for an equity audience.
The WGC's separate US Focus cut exists and is the relevant geography for this company, which the finding does not use.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: GOLD closed June at $41.32 and July at $39.35 - flat through and after the 2026-07-30 WGC release - then rallied 11.85% in August. There is no move in the tape attributable to this publication, which is what you would expect from data the market had already inferred from prices and premiums.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A US-specific WGC bar-and-coin figure showing a decline far worse than the global -36%, unreported in the coverage, would make this materially new.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The factual core is correct and I verified it independently: the 8-K exhibit for the Q2 FY2026 release (accession 0001193125-26-039858) reports diluted EPS of $0.46 on $6.477B revenue and net income of $11.6M, and the Tether release timestamped 2026-02-05 4:10pm EST discloses $150M at $44.50 for 3.371 million shares - roughly 12% of the company at an 11.9% discount to the 10-day VWAP - with the right to nominate a director. That two-event collision on one evening is real and the +9.87% is far more plausibly the PIPE than a $0.46 print. But both releases were in wire copy the same night and the following morning across GlobeNewswire, Yahoo Finance, Globe and Mail, Barchart, the Manila Times and Tether's own newsroom, so nothing here is undiscovered - this is a correction to a research artifact, and a market does not price a truncated CIK history. The inference the finding invites is also the part I would not accept: that this registrant produces small earnings reactions because the only 'clean' print moved +0.95%. The same operating business, same CIK, under the former name produced earnings-day moves of roughly -16%, -13% and +9% in the two years before the rename, including a 13% drop on the prior-year fiscal Q4 print. The rename on 2025-12-01 was cosmetic; the reaction distribution is not 1%. The option market agrees - 8.87% event-implied, 71% ATM IV - so if anything the finding's own conclusion is backwards, and its directional payload is zero either way.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Timestamped 4:10pm EST: Tether buys $150M of stock at $44.50, 3.371 million shares, with one board nomination right.
The same-evening Q2 FY2026 earnings exhibit: diluted EPS $0.46, revenue $6.477B, net income $11.6M - confirming the modest print alongside the PIPE.
Same-day mainstream coverage framing the news as Tether deepening metals exposure with a $150M investment - i.e. the market was told which of the two releases was the story.
Independent syndication of the PIPE release.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline itself records the 2026-02-05 move as +9.87% and the 52-week high of $66.70 four days later on 2026-02-09, which is a PIPE-and-momentum shape rather than an earnings shape. Against the finding, the baseline's own note that '13 earlier print(s) excluded as filed under a former name' identifies the excluded evidence that contradicts the finding's low-reaction conclusion.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the pre-rename AMRK earnings-day moves I found (-16%, -13%, +9%) turn out to be misattributed and the true former-name distribution is also near 1%, the finding's implication survives and this drops toward 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The gold price is the most continuously observed number in this sector and the August 2026 rally was front-page: Bloomberg ran 'Gold Miners Rally 33% in August as Debasement Trade Drives Investor Demand' on 2026-09-01, gold gained about 9.4% in the month from near $4,000 to a $4,633 peak, and the late-August give-back to $4,429 by 2026-08-31 on a hawkish Warsh Jackson Hole message was equally well covered. GOLD's own tape traded both legs in real time: +11.85% in August to a $47.25 high, then the baseline's run_up_5d of -6.81% as gold rolled over. That is the price already moving on this information twice, in the right direction and roughly the right size - which is the definition of priced. The finding also has a mechanism problem: the quarter being reported is the dead one, so the bullish content rests entirely on management's forward commentary on the call, not on the print, and a 4:30pm ET call is a separate event from the 4:05pm release the baseline is scored against. Finally its premium datum is selectively cut - it cites an 8.57% July average as a recovery while GOLD-1#1, using the same series, records 8.48% in July and 6.87% in August, so on the more recent month the two hunters agree the trend is down and this finding simply stops before it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Gold miners rallied 33% in August, the best August in decades, on the debasement trade - the rally the finding relies on, in a Bloomberg headline the day before the print.
The finding's own source: daily gold price coverage, i.e. the datum is published on a daily cadence by a mainstream outlet.
Gold's August rally ran into higher yields and a hawkish Fed, with futures at a near two-week low by early September and spot at $4,429 on 2026-08-31 - the give-back is also fully reported.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: August close $44.97 after a $47.25 high, +11.85% on the month, then run_up_5d of -6.81% into the print with spot at $43.66. The stock tracked gold up and back down within four weeks. run_up_20d of +2.27% is the residual. Skew is flat at +0.59 and put/call OI is 0.29, so no positioning asymmetry is left to exploit here.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Gold.com's Q1 FY2027 gross profit per ounce is decoupling upward from the gold price - for instance a published premium series showing September premiums back above 15% - would make the forward leg genuinely new.

interactions: Heavy overlap and one direct contradiction. (1) GOLD-2#0 is largely a re-packaging of GOLD-1#0 and GOLD-1#1: it re-states the May 2026 zero Silver Eagle print and the premium trough as supporting evidence, so scoring all three as independent would triple-count one retail-demand-collapse thesis. Its own added datum, WGC bar-and-coin tonnage, is the most published of the three and is framed by the publisher in the opposite direction ('held steady year-over-year'). (2) GOLD-1#1 and GOLD-2#2 rest on the same findbullionprices premium series and reach opposite conclusions about the same month: 1#1 reports 8.48% for July and 6.87% for August and calls it 'kept falling'; 2#2 reports an 8.57% July average and calls it a recovery from the 6.69% May trough. Both are anchor-dependent and both are consistent with August being below July, so 2#2's bullish reading survives only by stopping at July. (3) GOLD-1#0 and GOLD-1#3 both depend on the 2026-04-02 Sunshine Minting consolidation - 1#0 for the blank-supply exposure, 1#3 for the added cost base - so one publicly dated GlobeNewswire release underpins two findings. (4) GOLD-1#3 and GOLD-2#0 both hinge on the $2.09 versus $0.94-0.96 gap, which is the single most published fact about this print (it is the lede of the Investing.com preview dated today). (5) GOLD-2#1 is orthogonal to the other six - it corrects the baseline rather than the company - and its conclusion is undercut by the 13 pre-rename prints the baseline excluded, which include earnings-day moves near -16% and -13%; that is worth flagging to the caller because 2#1 tacitly argues for a smaller expected move while every other finding argues for a large one.
